items.passage: For decades, scientists assumed that sleep was simply a period of rest during which the brain switched off. Recent research, however, (1)---- that the sleeping brain is remarkably active. While we sleep, the hippocampus replays the experiences of the day, and the information (2)---- gradually transferred to the cortex for long-term storage. This process, known as consolidation, explains why students who sleep well after studying tend to remember more than those (3)---- stay up all night. (4)----, sleep appears to improve the ability to solve problems creatively, which may explain why difficult decisions often seem clearer in the morning. Researchers now hope that a better understanding of these mechanisms will help them to treat disorders (5)---- memory loss, such as Alzheimer's disease, more effectively.

items.passage: Antibiotics are among the most important discoveries in the history of medicine, yet their effectiveness is now under serious threat. items.passage: Procrastination is often dismissed as simple laziness, but psychologists argue that it is better understood as a problem of emotion regulation. items.passage: Few economic phenomena affect ordinary people as directly as inflation.
